description.value: This cross-sectional study compared recovering alcoholics with actively heavily drinking subjects using quantitative magnetic resonance imaging and proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging to assess regional brain volumes, white matter lesion volumes, gray matter volumes, and metabolite concentrations.

value: Recovering alcoholics had greater volumes of frontal white matter, but the opposite was true for white matter in a “remainder” region encompassing the basal frontal and temporal lobes, the cerebellum, and the brainstem.
The findings suggest region-specific structural recovery from chronic alcohol–induced brain injury, but also region-specific long-term structural damage in abstinent alcoholics.

value: Recovering alcoholics had smaller volumes of white matter lesions in whole brain, in occipital and mesial parietal regions, and in the remainder region.
White matter lesions were widespread in active drinkers and may partly resolve during long-term abstinence.
